6. Remarks and examples
Remark 5 (Extension to complex m). For each fixed n ≥1, both sides of (1) are rational
functions of m (after clearing the leading 1/m, they are polynomials in m of degree at most
n −1). The proof above establishes equality of these rational functions on the infinite set Z \ {0}
of nonzero integers. Two rational functions agreeing on an infinite set are equal as rational
functions, so (1) holds for every complex m ̸= 0 when both sides are interpreted as rational
functions of m.

Remark 9 (An infinite family of representations). As m ranges over Z \ {0}, (1) gives an infinite
family of distinct binomial-coefficient representations of Hn. By Remark 5, the family extends to
a single algebraic relation in the parameter m. The ”right” coefficient identities — those obtained
by extracting [mj] from the polynomial identity in Remark 5 — encode binomial sums for the
elementary symmetric polynomials in {1/1, 1/2, . . . , 1/n} and may merit further investigation.
